card.summary: subdomains under duckdns.org with a token API, IPv4, IPv6 and TXT support

free_tier.stated: subdomains under duckdns.org with a token API, IPv4, IPv6 and TXT support

per_object_cap.stated: the number of subdomains per account is about 5, a third-party figure; DuckDNS publishes no number

retention.stated: a record persists until updated or cleared with clear=true, provided the account is used

record.interface_detail: a single HTTPS GET per update; the token is a query parameter
record.tooling: curl, any DDNS client, a router's built-in DuckDNS provider
record.chaining: a name for a home IP or a tunnel endpoint, and nothing else: no certificate automation and no proxying

limits.value: about 5 subdomains, a third-party figure; DuckDNS publishes no number

record.reliability_note: a bad token returns HTTP 200 with the body KO, so a status-only check reports success on a failed update
record.confidence_note: the update endpoint was called today with an empty token and answered 200 KO, which proves both the endpoint and the failure shape. The subdomain cap is third-party.

evidence.proved: 200 with a two-byte body 'KO'. A 200 is not success; the rejection is in the body
the update URL, IPv4 and IPv6 parameters, the TXT form, and clear=true to delete records; a TXT record applies to all sub-subdomains under the name
the update is a single HTTPS GET to DuckDNS
evidence.quote: You can update your domain(s) with a single HTTPS get to DuckDNS

evidence.proved: clear=true makes the update call clear the IPv4 and IPv6 values of the named subnames instead of setting them
evidence.quote: clear - OPTIONAL - if set to true, the update will ignore all ip's and clear both your records

evidence.proved: the update call is a GET to duckdns.org/update with the subnames and the account token as query parameters

record.notes: A DuckDNS name cannot be a Cloudflare zone, so it cannot carry a Tunnel, Email Routing or Universal SSL. It is a dynamic-DNS tool, not a name a service can live on.
